newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese journalist charged with Israel contacts.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese journalist charged with Israel contacts.

text.p: Lebanon's military prosecuter charged on Monday a journalist with having contacts with Israel and distributing leaflets that incite military disobedience.
Nasri Lahoud said in an indictment that Christian journalist Pierre Atallah and another man, Ghassan Bardaweel, were also charged with "disturbing Lebanon's relation with a friendly country".
Atallah of Beirut's leading conservative An-Nahar newspaper, Bardaweel and 46 others were detained in a recent widespread campaign which took place in the last two weeks.
The detention campaign was sparked by an incident in which a van carrying Syrian workers was machinegunned in a predominently Christian area, killing the driver and injuring some passengers.
Syria has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.
Many detainees have been released and two others are still in custody waiting to have their legal situation settled within 24 hours, Lahoud said. He did not mention the number of those released.
Atallah was also charged with "making contacts with the Israeli enemy agents and distributing leaflets that incite soldiers against obeying orders".
If convicted with these charges, Atallah and Bardaweel face up to three years in prison.
